# Architecture {#sec-en-architecture}

[🇩🇪 Auf Deutsch lesen](../de/architecture.html){.btn .btn-sm .btn-outline-secondary style="float:right"}

This chapter describes the overall system design of gdrive-fuse: component
structure, data flows, and the interaction between the kernel, FUSE library,
and Google Drive API.

## System Overview

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-en-system-overview
%%| fig-cap: "System overview: Kernel ↔ FUSE ↔ Google Drive"
graph TB
    subgraph Kernel["Linux Kernel"]
        VFS["VFS (Virtual File System)"]
        FUSE_K["fuse.ko (Kernel Module)"]
    end

    subgraph Userspace["User Space"]
        subgraph App["Application (shell, editor, …)"]
            Syscall["open / read / readdir / stat …"]
        end

        subgraph Client["gdrive-fuse (C++ or Rust)"]
            FuseLib["FUSE3 Library<br/>(libfuse3 / fuser)"]
            FuseOps["FuseOps<br/>(Callback Handler)"]
            Cache["Cache Layer<br/>(Dir + Content)"]
            GClient["GClient<br/>(Drive REST API)"]
            Auth["Auth<br/>(OAuth2)"]
            Watcher["Change Watcher<br/>(Drive Changes API)"]
        end
    end

    subgraph Cloud["Google Cloud"]
        DriveAPI["Google Drive API v3"]
        OAuth["OAuth2 Token Endpoint"]
    end

    Syscall -->|POSIX syscall| VFS
    VFS <-->|/dev/fuse| FUSE_K
    FUSE_K <-->|messages| FuseLib
    FuseLib --> FuseOps
    FuseOps --> Cache
    Cache -->|cache miss| GClient
    GClient -->|REST HTTP/2| DriveAPI
    Auth -->|token| GClient
    Auth <-->|code flow + refresh| OAuth
    Watcher -->|invalidation| Cache
    Watcher <-->|Changes API| DriveAPI
```

## Component Descriptions

### Auth

`Auth` encapsulates the full OAuth2 Authorization Code Flow for desktop
applications:

1. Generates a one-time *state* parameter (CSRF protection).
2. Opens the authorization URL in the default browser.
3. Starts a temporary HTTP server on `localhost:8080` and waits for the
   callback with the authorization code.
4. Exchanges the code for access and refresh tokens.
5. Persists the tokens in `~/.gdrive_tokens.json` (protected by file system
   permissions).
6. Automatically renews the access token before expiry using the refresh token.

Token access is protected internally by a mutex (C++) or
`parking_lot::RwLock` (Rust).

### GClient

`GClient` is a stateless HTTP wrapper around the Google Drive REST API v3:

| Method | Drive Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `listFiles(parent_id)` | `GET /files` | Fetch directory contents |
| `revalidateDir(id, etag)` | `GET /files` (If-None-Match) | Conditional fetch |
| `getFileMetadata(id)` | `GET /files/{id}` | File metadata |
| `downloadFile(id)` | `GET /files/{id}?alt=media` | Download file content |
| `uploadFile(name, data, parent)` | `POST /upload/drive/v3/files` | Upload file |
| `deleteFile(id)` | `DELETE /files/{id}` | Delete file |
| `getStartPageToken()` | `GET /changes/startPageToken` | Initial changes token |
| `pollChanges(token)` | `GET /changes` | Poll for changes |

All methods are **blocking (synchronous)** — no async runtime is needed within
the FUSE context.

### Cache Layer (FuseOps / ObjectManager)

The cache is three-tiered:

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-en-cache-layers
%%| fig-cap: "Three cache tiers"
graph LR
    subgraph L1["Path-ID Cache"]
        P["path → Drive ID"]
    end
    subgraph L2["Metadata Cache"]
        M["Drive ID → FileInfo"]
    end
    subgraph L3["Content Cache"]
        C["Drive ID → bytes<br/>(LRU, ≤ 1 GiB)"]
    end
    subgraph L4["Directory Cache"]
        D["Drive ID → DirListing<br/>+ ETag + state"]
    end
    FuseOps --> L1
    L1 --> L2
    L2 --> L3
    L2 --> L4
```

#### Directory Cache: 3-State Machine

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-en-cache-state
%%| fig-cap: "Directory cache state machine"
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> INVALID : first access / after write operation
    INVALID --> FRESH : listFiles() succeeds
    FRESH --> STALE : TTL (30 s) expires
    STALE --> FRESH : revalidateDir() → 304 Not Modified
    STALE --> FRESH : revalidateDir() → 200 (new data)
    FRESH --> INVALID : change-watcher fires
    STALE --> INVALID : change-watcher fires
```

### FUSE Operations (FuseOps / GDriveFuse)

`FuseOps` (C++) and `GDriveFuse` (Rust) implement the FUSE callbacks:

| FUSE Operation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `getattr` | Cache lookup → on miss: fetch metadata from Drive |
| `readdir` | Check dir cache → FRESH: serve directly; STALE: revalidate; INVALID: reload |
| `read` | Check content cache → on miss: download and cache (if ≤ 1 MiB) |

All FUSE callbacks catch exceptions and return POSIX error codes
(`-ENOENT`, `-EIO`, …).

### Change Watcher

The background thread polls the Drive Changes API periodically and invalidates
affected cache entries:

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-en-watcher-flow
%%| fig-cap: "Change watcher flow"
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as Change Watcher
    participant G as GClient
    participant C as Cache

    W->>G: getStartPageToken()
    G-->>W: pageToken₀

    loop every N seconds
        W->>G: pollChanges(pageTokenₙ)
        G-->>W: [ChangeList, pageTokenₙ₊₁]
        alt Changes detected
            W->>C: invalidateDirCache(affected IDs)
        end
    end
```

## Concurrency Model

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-en-concurrency
%%| fig-cap: "Threading model (Rust client)"
graph TB
    subgraph FUSE["FUSE Thread (fuser)"]
        FT["GDriveFuse::lookup<br/>GDriveFuse::readdir<br/>GDriveFuse::read<br/>…"]
    end
    subgraph Workers["Worker Pool"]
        W1["Worker 1<br/>(High Priority)"]
        W2["Worker 2<br/>(Normal)"]
        W3["Workers 3–N<br/>(Low / Prefetch)"]
    end
    subgraph State["Shared State"]
        OM["ObjectManager<br/>(DashMap — sharded RwLock)"]
        QM["QueueManager<br/>(crossbeam-channel)"]
    end
    subgraph BG["Background Threads"]
        CW["Change Watcher"]
        SP["Startup Prefetch"]
    end

    FT -->|"enqueue_and_wait (blocking)"| QM
    FT -->|"cache reads"| OM
    QM --> W1
    QM --> W2
    QM --> W3
    W1 -->|"store_* methods"| OM
    W2 -->|"store_* methods"| OM
    W3 -->|"store_* methods"| OM
    CW -->|"invalidate_dir"| OM
    SP -->|"enqueue (fire-and-forget)"| QM
```

In the **C++ client**, a `std::shared_mutex` (`cache_mutex_`) plays the role
of the DashMap shards: `shared_lock` for concurrent reads, `unique_lock` for
writes. Per-file downloads are serialised via a separate `file_mutexes_`
registry without holding `cache_mutex_`.

## Data Flow for a File Read

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-en-read-flow
%%| fig-cap: "Data flow: read() syscall to file content"
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant Kernel
    participant FuseOps
    participant Cache
    participant QueueMgr
    participant GClient
    participant Drive as Google Drive API

    User->>Kernel: read(fd, buf, n)
    Kernel->>FuseOps: read(path, buf, n, offset)
    FuseOps->>Cache: get_content(file_id)
    alt Cache hit
        Cache-->>FuseOps: bytes
    else Cache miss
        FuseOps->>QueueMgr: enqueue_and_wait(DownloadFile)
        QueueMgr->>GClient: downloadFile(file_id)
        GClient->>Drive: GET /files/{id}?alt=media
        Drive-->>GClient: bytes
        GClient-->>QueueMgr: bytes
        QueueMgr->>Cache: store_content(file_id, bytes)
        QueueMgr-->>FuseOps: TaskResult::Ok
        FuseOps->>Cache: get_content(file_id)
        Cache-->>FuseOps: bytes
    end
    FuseOps-->>Kernel: n bytes
    Kernel-->>User: data
```
